subject: Chemistry
title: REACH: Europe's Chemical Safety Law
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: REACH: Europe's Chemical Safety Law.

hook.text: Before 2007, chemicals could be sold in Europe without proving they were safe. REACH reversed the burden of proof.

buildup.text: REACH stands for Registration, Evaluation, Authorization, and Restriction of Chemicals. It covers 30,000+ substances.

discovery.text: Companies must now prove a chemical is safe before selling it. Previously, regulators had to prove it was dangerous.

twist.text: REACH identified 224 'substances of very high concern'—including chemicals in everyday products used for decades.

climax.text: The regulation costs industry €2.1 billion yearly but prevents an estimated €50 billion in health and environmental damage.

punchline.text: Prove it's safe first, then sell it. A simple idea that took disasters to learn.

quiz.question: How did REACH change chemical regulation in Europe?
options: Companies must prove chemicals are safe before selling, not after harm is found
It banned all synthetic chemicals from consumer products
It required all chemicals to be tested on animals first

details.summary: REACH is the European Union's comprehensive chemicals regulation requiring manufacturers to register, evaluate, and authorize chemicals before they can be sold..
details.whyItMatters: REACH fundamentally changed the global chemicals market by requiring safety data for tens of thousands of chemicals that had been sold for decades without toxicity testing.
takeaways: REACH requires safety data for all chemicals sold above one ton annually
It shifted the burden of proof from regulators to manufacturers
The regulation has driven global chemical safety improvements beyond Europe

faq.question: How does REACH differ from chemical regulation in the United States?
faq.answer: REACH requires companies to prove chemicals are safe before market entry. The US Toxic Substances Control Act historically grandfathered existing chemicals and required the EPA to prove harm before restricting them..

faq.question: Has REACH actually improved chemical safety in Europe?
faq.answer: Yes. REACH has generated safety data for over 23,000 chemicals, restricted over 200 hazardous substances, and driven substitution of dangerous chemicals with safer alternatives. It has also influenced chemical regulations in countries like South Korea, Turkey, and the UK post-Brexit.
